name: Washington

context: WA PM TN 14: Three wind erosion periods in potatoes: after fall fumigation, after spring planting, and after harvest.
WA PM TN 14: After fumigation, wind speeds exceed 60 mph are common and residue left is too little to protect the soil.
WA 329: Maintain a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year (for plant-available moisture).
cover_rules: WA 340: Time cover crop establishment with other practices so the soil is protected during the critical erosion periods.
WA PM TN 14: Delaying fall seeding even a few days can greatly reduce ground cover; raising the seeding rate is not as effective as early seeding.
WA 340: Use current erosion prediction technology to set the surface and canopy cover the cover crop must give.
residue: WA 329: Keep a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
WA 329: Minimum stubble height when significant snowfall is expected: at least 10 inches for row spacing under 15 inches, 15 inches for 15 inches or greater.
WA 345: Residue should not be shredded after harvest; shredding makes it more open to movement by wind or water.
barriers: WA 603: Herbaceous wind barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing no more than 10 times barrier height.
WA 589: Cross wind trap strips are at least 15 feet wide if stubble is 1 foot or more in height, and at least 25 feet if shorter.
WA 588: Cross wind ridges stay within 45 degrees of perpendicular to the wind; spacing no more than 4 times ridge height.
windbreak: WA 380: Protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side; orient the windbreak perpendicular to the erosive wind.
WA 380: Select species for planting that are taller than the height of the crop; design for function within 20 years.
roughening: WA 609: Emergency tillage that makes random roughness large enough for a 25% reduction in potential erosion rate.
WA 609: Not a primary control; use when a planned wind erosion control system fails during a high wind event.
WA 588: On loamy sand and sand soils, establish cross wind ridges when soil is moist; ridges on these soils deteriorate quickly.
grazing: WA 528: Plan grazing to leave adequate ground cover from canopy, litter and trampled residue to protect soil from wind and water.
WA 528: Minimize grazing animal impact on areas that have high soil erosion potential.
WA 528: Provide adequate rest to enhance regrowth of desirable species.
WA 528: Locate fences and watering facilities away from erosion-prone areas.
drought: WA 528: Develop and document contingencies for episodic disturbances such as drought.
WA 528: Use drought and other weather forecasting tools to match forage production and grazing.
seeding: WA 550: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis.
WA PM TN 15: Broadcast seeding requires doubling the seeding rate.
WA PM TN 2: Rates target 20-30 seeds/ft2 for larger seeds and 40-50 seeds/ft2 for smaller seeds, PLS basis, 12-inch rows.
dont_seed: WA PM TN 14: Planting too late in the fall should be avoided; it fails to protect the soil.
WA PM TN 15: Hoe openers should be discouraged because of inadequate control of seed depth placement.
WA PM TN 2: Avoid shallow and sandy soils for orchardgrass.
pasture: WA 512: Select plants that provide maximum ground cover for protection of the soil from wind and water erosion.
WA 512: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis.
WA PM TN 2: Tall wheatgrass pure stand rate is 10 lb/ac on good soils; increase to 15 lb/ac on saline soils.
crp: WA PM TN 15: Perennial grass species, such as the wheatgrasses, are the recommended cover for most CRP acreage in Washington.
WA PM TN 15: Broadcast seeding requires doubling the seeding rate; fall germinating cheatgrass must be controlled first.
WA PM TN 15: Hoe openers are discouraged because of inadequate seed depth control (relatively HIGH risk).
disturbed: WA 342: Mulch or otherwise stabilize (e.g., polyacrylamide (PAM)) plantings as necessary to ensure successful establishment.
WA 342: Specify species, rates of seeding or planting, and dates based on local planting guides.
WA 342: Applies to highly disturbed areas where erosion by wind or water is high.
dunes: WA 342: Dune plants must survive burial by blowing sand, sand blasting, drought, heat, and low nutrient supply.
WA 342: Include sand trapping devices such as sand fences or brush matting in the stabilization plan.
WA PM TN 14: Straw mulch reduces wind erosion providing the straw is firmly anchored.

coverPlant.text: WA PM TN 14: October 20th has typically been the cut-off date for fall cover crop seedings in central Washington.
WA PM TN 14: Cereal rye is planted Late Aug.-Late Oct.; winter wheat Late Sept.-Late Oct.

seedWin.text: WA PM TN 14: October 20th has typically been the cut-off date for fall cover crop seedings in central Washington.
WA PM TN 15: For CRP grass seeding, wait until after fall rains settle the soil and fall germinating cheatgrass is controlled.

avoid: Species on Federal or State invasive species or noxious weed lists
Plants that may be alternate hosts to undesirable pests
Species with shade, allelopathy, competing roots or root sprouts that hurt the crop
